items.question: How does consciousness manifest beings without division?
premises: Consciousness opens forth by its own forceful surge.
It makes the portions of beings shine.
It shines them without division and as non-different from itself.
items.inference: Self-manifesting consciousness reveals all beings as undivided and identical with itself.
items.plain_english: Thus, by the force of its own surge, consciousness opens forth by itself and, without division, makes the portions of beings shine as non-different from its own self.

items.question: What happens when consciousness does not sink into closure?
premises: Consciousness may for a moment not become an object of closing.
From that, māyā dissolves.
When māyā dissolves, the Bhairava level shines forth.
items.inference: A brief non-closure of consciousness dissolves māyā and reveals the Bhairava state.
items.plain_english: If, even for a moment, it does not sink into closure, then through the dissolving of māyā the level of Bhairava shines forth.

rows.grounds: optative of dṛś in causative sense

items.question: What is the source of the appearance of division?
premises: A limitation born of conceptualization may afterward show division.
That very showing of division is māyā.
Māyā belongs to the free one and reveals a vision of difference.
items.inference: The appearance of division is māyā, a power of the free absolute that manifests difference.
items.plain_english: For the limitation born of conceptualization may afterward show division; that very division is māyā, the power of the free one that reveals the vision of difference.

items.question: Can māyā arise for one established in pure opening?
premises: For one established only in the opening of consciousness, māyā is rootless.
What is rootless cannot arise.
In the method of the unsurpassed self, much explanation is unnecessary.
items.inference: In the unsurpassed self, māyā cannot arise for one abiding in pure opening.
items.plain_english: For one who rests only in the opening of consciousness, that māyā is rootless and cannot arise; so what is the use of saying more in this method of the unsurpassed self?

rows.grounds: asti with initial a elided in text

items.question: Can any limb of yoga truly serve as a means here?
premises: In reality no limb of yoga has the status of a means.
The own nature of this reality is without form.
It is without form because it is free from limitation.
items.inference: Since the reality is formless and unlimited, no yogic limb can function as a true means to it.
items.plain_english: In reality, no limb of yoga can serve as a means, for its own nature is formless, being free from all limitation.

rows.grounds: refers to the state or practice

items.question: Why is the means here also not a means?
premises: This means is also a non-means because it blocks effortful activity.
It is devoid of exhalation and inhalation practices.
It is devoid of regulation of body and breath.
items.inference: The so-called means transcends ordinary technique by abandoning effortful bodily and breath controls.
uncertainties: The exact analysis of tanuvātanauḥ is compressed in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: Even the means is not a means, because it stops effortful activity; it is free from exhalation and inhalation and from the regulation of body and breath.

rows.grounds: present of tṛ in causative sense

items.question: How can the mind cross over while immersed in objects?
premises: The self may be sinking in the ocean of difference.
Even then, this mind can carry the self across.
This occurs even while the mind is in an object-bound taste.
items.inference: The mind, rightly oriented, can rescue the self from difference even amid sensory immersion.
items.plain_english: Thus this mind carries the self across from the ocean of difference, even when it is sinking while still in the taste of objects.

items.question: Why does forcibly restraining the mind fail to soften it inwardly?
premises: A gourd without holes does not become inwardly soft.
Some people restrain the mind's own path as one restrains a horse.
Such forced restraint does not produce inner receptivity.
items.inference: Forcible suppression of the mind does not create inner openness, just as a sealed gourd does not soften.
items.plain_english: A gourd without holes does not become soft inside; likewise, those who forcibly restrain the mind's own path, as if holding back a horse, do not make it inwardly receptive.

items.question: What happens to the mind when it is forcibly broken?
premises: For those who practice breaking the mind, it runs off by countless wrong paths.
The mind keeps asking what this is.
Even in pain, the mind mostly longs restlessly.
items.inference: Suppressing the mind scatters it into wrong paths and restless craving rather than settling it.
items.plain_english: For those who try to break the mind, it runs off along countless wrong paths; wondering, 'What is this?', the mind mostly keeps longing restlessly, even in pain.

items.question: How does knowledge produce dispassion even toward pleasure?
premises: Through knowledge one may become dispassionate even toward pleasure.
Knowledge clarifies this and that as they are.
The teacher has instructed this in many ways in his own teaching.
items.inference: True dispassion arises from knowledge, as the teacher repeatedly taught.
items.plain_english: Through knowledge one can become dispassionate even toward pleasure, discerning 'this is this'; for the teacher has taught this in many ways in his own scripture.

items.question: What makes the activities of the senses fall away naturally?
premises: Sense activities fall away through indifference and dispassion alone.
When they are forcibly controlled, they do not settle.
As long as they are controlled by force, they act turbulently.
items.inference: Natural dispassion quiets the senses, while forcible control agitates them.
items.plain_english: The activities of the senses fall away through indifference and dispassion alone; but as long as they are forcibly controlled, they keep acting turbulently.

rows.grounds: akṣa+jāla compound with initial a elided

items.question: Is forced sensory withdrawal a true release from bondage?
premises: There is a so-called withdrawal applied to the net of the senses.
When bondage is already firmly established, such withdrawal is imposed on it.
That imposed withdrawal becomes a binding like diamond cement.
items.inference: Forced pratyāhāra, applied over established bondage, strengthens bondage rather than removing it.
items.plain_english: Even that so-called withdrawal which is applied to the net of the senses becomes, for one whose bondage is already firmly set, a binding as hard as diamond cement.

rows.grounds: present participle of ā+viś with negation

items.question: How can one know inner ease amid objects and experiences?
premises: One may be amid objects, their enjoyment, and the pleasure or pain arising from them.
Even while immersed in mind, one may not enter them with fear.
In that state, one knows the inner ease of the dissolution of mental activities.
items.inference: Freedom from fearful identification allows one to know inner stillness even amid experience.
uncertainties: The backslash tokens are preserved as editorial line-break markers from the source list.
items.plain_english: Amid objects, their enjoyment, and the pleasure or pain that arises from them, those whose fear has dissolved, though their minds are immersed, do not truly enter into them and know within the ease of the quieting of mental activity.

rows.grounds: locative plural participle form as given

items.question: What reality should be accepted when senses and objects are fully present?
premises: The self shines in the heart as the great light of consciousness.
The senses and objects such as taste may still be present and active.
A yogi can abide clearly in a state whose arising is barren of difference and filled with fullness.
items.inference: Even amid active senses and objects, the yogi should accept the nondual reality of consciousness.
items.plain_english: When the self, the great light of consciousness, is present in the heart, and the senses and objects such as taste are also present and active, the yogi abides very clearly in a fullness whose arising is free of difference; let that reality be accepted.

items.question: Is non-discrimination only bondage or also a means to liberation?
premises: It is commonly said that non-discrimination is supreme bondage.
That common saying is only a partial report.
Non-discrimination itself can become the supreme stairway to gaining liberation.
items.inference: Non-discrimination is not merely bondage; rightly understood, it can serve as the path to liberation.
items.plain_english: To say that non-discrimination is supreme bondage is only a common saying; for non-discrimination itself can be the supreme stairway to attaining liberation.

rows.grounds: tyaja+avadhānāni fused in text, command plus object

items.question: Where can deliberate concentration truly be placed?
premises: One is told to abandon deliberate concentrations.
In the full, concentration is not fitting.
In the not-full, concentration does not attain true being.
items.inference: Deliberate concentration cannot establish truth in either fullness or incompleteness, so it should be abandoned.
items.plain_english: Abandon deliberate concentrations; where, indeed, would you place concentration? Examine it yourself: in the full it is not fitting, and in the not-full it does not attain true being.

rows.grounds: editorial lacuna marker in token list
editorial lacuna marker in token list

items.question: Where can the yogi realize fullness amid all states of activity?
premises: Wherever union with bliss arises, there the own nature is full.
If the delusion of difference is known, one may reach peace there.
Even in waking and all states, the yogi can become lord of the great wheel of consciousness while active.
items.inference: Recognizing bliss and dispelling the delusion of difference allows the yogi to realize fullness in every state.
uncertainties: The two '---' tokens mark a lacuna in the transmitted text.
The fragmentary sequence 'te veti' is preserved as given and may be textually uncertain.
items.plain_english: Wherever union with bliss arises, there one's own nature is full; if the delusion of difference is understood, one may reach peace there. Even in waking and in every state, the yogi can become the lord of the great wheel of consciousness, moving through varied activities while shining with mantra power.

items.question: Why do people attain the supreme in different ways?
premises: One person digging a well feels accomplished only when water is reached.
Another is satisfied with water already at hand.
The attainment of the supreme likewise follows varied ways.
items.inference: The method of attaining the supreme differs according to readiness and circumstance.
items.plain_english: Just as one who sets out to dig a well feels accomplished only when water is reached, while another is satisfied with water already in hand, so the way of attaining the supreme is varied.

items.question: How can a person be freed from the bondage of difference?
premises: This reality is without means.
Ordinary thinking relies on the connection of means and goal.
The question remains how a person is freed from the bondage of difference.
items.inference: Since the reality is beyond means, liberation from difference cannot be explained by ordinary means-and-goal logic.
items.plain_english: This is without means; so how, by the usual relation of means and goal, or in any other way, could a person be freed from the bondage of difference?

items.question: Why does the scripture teach means if the reality is without means?
premises: The reality itself is without means.
Still, instruction can operate by relational functioning.
This scripture therefore teaches means in many ways.
items.inference: Scriptural means are taught provisionally, by relation, even though the ultimate reality is beyond means.
items.plain_english: Even though this reality is without means, this scripture teaches means in many ways, functioning through relational instruction.

items.question: How do provisional means lead the deluded toward the real?
premises: Children are led clearly into the real nature of sound through written letters.
The letters are provisional aids, not the final reality.
In the same way, the deluded are led gradually by provisional means.
items.inference: Provisional means function pedagogically to lead the unprepared toward the real.
items.plain_english: Just as children are clearly led into the real nature of sound through written letters, so the deluded are gradually led by those provisional means.

items.question: Why does a nondual scripture still teach worship and meditation?
premises: The supreme reality is nondual.
Even so, provisional instruction is needed for that purpose.
Therefore this scripture respectfully teaches worship, meditation, and related practices.
items.inference: Nondual teaching can include provisional practices as skillful means for realization.
items.plain_english: For that very purpose, even in the nondual supreme reality, this scripture respectfully teaches something appropriate, such as worship and meditation.

items.question: How can any pleasing sensory state become a path to realization?
premises: Anything that delights the mind may arise in any state of the senses.
That delight can be joined to the abode of true awareness.
It can be joined to the opening of Brahman.
items.inference: Any mind-delighting sensory experience can become a support for realization when joined to the abode of awareness.
items.plain_english: Whatever delights the mind, in any state of the senses, can be joined to the abode of true awareness, to the very opening of Brahman.

items.question: How does ordinary experience become effortless worship of the supreme powers?
premises: Absorption in true being follows the self.
That absorption supports the rite of worship of the wheel of supreme Kula powers.
Through this, experience naturally becomes an instrument without effort.
items.inference: When grounded in absorption in true being, experience effortlessly becomes worship of the supreme powers.
items.plain_english: Resting on absorption in true being that follows the self, one naturally and without effort comes to function as an instrument in the worship of the wheel of the supreme Kula lord and his powers.
